title: Semantic audit payload guidance for SIEM and evidence automation
content:
Purpose and scope:

This note proposes a concise, semantics-first payload shape for audit events that is optimized for two operational consumers: (1) evidence automation and forensic reconstruction, and (2) SIEM export/analysis pipelines. The goal is to limit per-event size, preserve causal ordering, enable efficient backfill/replay, and provide a clear mapping to RBAC v2 context without leaking sensitive data into SIEM exports.

Principles (high-level):
- Single source of truth: the internal audit event (master payload) must be canonical for evidence reconstruction. All downstream exports (SIEM/third-party) are derived transforms, not the authoritative records.
- Compact semantic fields: use short, stable keys but include a small set of explicit semantic fields rather than free text blobs.
- Causality and replayable ordering: every event carries monotonic sequencing and provenance metadata to allow deterministic replay.
- RBAC context enrichment: attach minimal role/entitlement descriptors to allow fast filtering and alerting in SIEM without exporting full entitlement graphs.
- PII minimization for SIEM: implement transform rules to remove or hash PII before export while preserving linkability to evidence references.

Recommended top-level payload (master audit event)
- event_id: global UUID (v4) as the canonical identifier for the event
- occurred_at: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp (source-system time)
- observed_at: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp when the audit pipeline accepted the event (useful for clock skew detection)
- schema_version: short version string (semi-semantic), e.g. "audit/2025-01-01.v1"
- actor: compact actor object (see below)
- action: short verb, namespaced where appropriate (e.g. "model.deploy.start", "route.update")
- outcome: enum [success, failure, denied, error, noop]
- resource: compact resource reference (type + id + optional human label)
- rbac_context: minimal RBAC v2 snapshot (see section)
- sequence: {stream_id, seq_no, prev_seq_id} (see sequencing section)
- evidence_refs: list of stable evidence references (URLs or artifact ids)
- telemetry: small key/value bag for internal metrics (optional)
- raw_payload_location: provable pointer to the full event payload in evidence store (S3/GCS/ark)

Notes on fields and rationale
- schema_version: include the date and a minor version so that downstream consumers can assert compatibility. Avoid ISO timestamps for micro-versions.
- actor: must be limited to fields necessary to identify the subject without embedding a full profile. Suggested actor keys: {id, type, display_name, anon_id_hash}. The anon_id_hash is a one-way SHA256 of actor.id + salt used before SIEM export to preserve linkability without PHI.
- action: small vocabulary; adopt a canonical action registry within the security team. Prefer dotted names and avoid long descriptions.
- resource: include resource.type (e.g., model, deployment, route, key), resource.id, and optional label. Avoid embedding resource metadata that contains secrets.
- rbac_context: include roles (short role ids), role_source (e.g., org-claim, external-iam), and access_reason (optional freeform string when access was elevated via support workflow). Do NOT include full entitlement tree.

Sequencing and ordering model
- stream_id: logical shard for ordering (e.g., tenant-<org_id> or global-ingest-partition-#)
- seq_no: monotonically increasing integer within stream_id assigned by producer or ingestion gateway
- prev_seq_id: event_id of prior event in the same logical sequence where available (null for head)
- monotonic_token (optional): an increasing wall-clock token provided by the ingestion service for cross-stream correlation

Why sequencing matters:
- Enables deterministic reconstruction for forensic timelines.
- Helps implement idempotent backfills: when replaying events, seq_no + stream_id + event_id should be used to dedupe.

Example master event (stringified JSON for illustration):

{
  "event_id": "f3a9b7f6-8c9a-4e6f-9b01-2a3c4d5e6f77",
  "occurred_at": "2025-01-15T18:41:03.123Z",
  "observed_at": "2025-01-15T18:41:03.983Z",
  "schema_version": "audit/2025-01-01.v1",
  "actor": {
    "id": "user:uplift:241",
    "type": "user",
    "display_name": "a.chen",
    "anon_id_hash": "sha256:6b1f..."
  },
  "action": "model.deploy.start",
  "outcome": "success",
  "resource": {
    "type": "model",
    "id": "mdl-rw-7k3"
  },
  "rbac_context": {
    "roles": ["se-deployer"],
    "role_source": "org-claim"
  },
  "sequence": {
    "stream_id": "tenant-231",
    "seq_no": 12345
  },
  "evidence_refs": ["s3://redwood-audit/2025/01/15/f3a9b7f6.json"],
  "raw_payload_location": "s3://redwood-audit/raw-events/5e6f77.gz"
}

Note: the master event's raw_payload_location may point to a compressed JSONL that contains a richer payload (stack traces, full request/response bodies) retained in cold storage for forensic retrieval.

SIEM export transform rules (derived view)
- Keep: event_id, occurred_at (rename to @timestamp for ECS compatibility), actor.anon_id_hash, action, outcome, resource.type/id, minimal roles list, sequence.stream_id, sequence.seq_no, evidence_refs pointers (if allowed), and a sanitized message_short.
- Remove or hash: actor.display_name and any user email/phone fields; strip request/response bodies; remove raw_payload_location unless export policy allows.
- Pseudonymization: use keyed HMAC for any identifier exported to SIEM. Keys are rotated quarterly and stored in KMS. Exports must record used key version in the export manifest.
- Flattening: produce ECS-friendly top-level fields: (ecs.version, host.name, event.dataset="redwood.audit" ) in addition to our derived fields.

Example SIEM-compatible event (conceptual):

{
  "@timestamp": "2025-01-15T18:41:03.123Z",
  "event_id": "f3a9b7f6-8c9a-4e6f-9b01-2a3c4d5e6f77",
  "event.dataset": "redwood.audit",
  "event.action": "model.deploy.start",
  "event.outcome": "success",
  "user.id_hmac": "hmac:v2:a7c1...",
  "rbac.roles": ["se-deployer"],
  "resource.type": "model",
  "resource.id": "mdl-rw-7k3",
  "sequence.stream_id": "tenant-231",
  "sequence.seq_no": 12345
}

Retention, redaction and export policy guidance
- Master events: retain full (raw) payload for 2 years in cold storage; short metadata retained hot for 90 days.
- SIEM exports: 90 day retention on SIEM side (respecting customer/region rules).
- Redaction policy: implement a redaction annotation list in raw payloads (evidence store) so that if a request contains PII it is tagged with redaction reasons and retention exceptions.
- Export gating: SIEM exports must run through a policy filter that enforces per-tenant opt-outs and per-region compliance (e.g., EU requires extra hashing).

Migration and versioning strategy (v1 -> v2 -> v3)
- Backward compatibility: Additive fields only; deprecate by marking fields as deprecated in schema_version but keep them for N months.
- Dual-write window: producers should dual-write master payload (new schema) and a compat payload for at least 30 days. During this window consumers are updated to consume the new schema.
- Backfill plan for historical events: use ingestion gateway to compute sequence tokens and populate sequence.{stream_id,seq_no} when missing. Backfill jobs must be idempotent and operate in time-bounded batches (e.g., 7d windows).
- Validation: implement a lightweight per-event JSON schema check at ingress that rejects malformed events and returns clear error codes. Rejected events go to quarantine queue for manual triage.

Evidence automation implications
- Evidence_refs should be stable, content-addressed (sha256 prefix) when possible to ensure immutability.
- Automation consumers should prefer raw_payload_location slices that contain an evidence manifest describing what was redacted and why.
- Support sealed evidence: for high-compliance tenants, support a signed manifest (KMS-signed) that proves the event contents at a point-in-time.

Operational checklist for rollout
1) Publish canonical action registry and role short-ids (security team)
2) Implement ingestion schema enforcement in the gateway, return clear errors to producers
3) Add sequence assignment to the ingestion gateway; start dual-writing sequence fields for new events
4) Implement SIEM transform service that applies pseudonymization and ECS flattening
5) Run a 6-week dual-write + consumer upgrade period, then toggle old compat writes off
6) Schedule backfill tasks for any historical events missing sequence tokens; run in low-traffic windows

Open questions / decisions needed
- Key rotation cadence for HMAC pseudonymization and export manifest format.
- Allowed evidence_refs in SIEM by default: should we include pointers or strip them by default?
- Role snapshot depth: how many roles should we export in rbac_context by default (top-3, or full list)?

Appendix: quick field glossary
- event_id (string): global uuid for event
- occurred_at (timestamp): when action took place
- observed_at (timestamp): when ingestion saw it
- schema_version (string): version token for compatibility
- actor.id (string): internal actor id
- actor.anon_id_hash (string): one-way hash used in exports
- action (string): canonical action verb
- outcome (string): result enum
- resource.type/id (string): small resource reference
- rbac_context.roles (array): short role ids
- sequence.stream_id (string): ordering shard id
- sequence.seq_no (integer): per-shard sequence number
- evidence_refs (array): stable pointers to evidence artifacts

This note is intentionally prescriptive but lightweight. The next steps are to get sign-off on the action registry and the pseudonymization key policy, add an ingestion schema validator, and build the SIEM transform as an independent service so it can be iterated on without touching the master audit store.

Comments and review: please annotate inline with your expected consumer concerns (SIEM, SRE, SRE-sre, platform, legal).
